newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore non-oil exports down 2.1 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Singapore non-oil exports down 2.1 pct in March.

text.p: Singapore exports of non-oil goods fell a nominal 2.1 percent year-on-year in March to Singapore $7.67 billion (US$5.33 billion), after falling 7.9 percent in February, the Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Monday.
In real terms, non-oil exports rose 0.5 percent in March to S$9.88 billion after falling 4.4 percent in February.
The figures were slightly better than expected.
A Reuters poll of 11 economists last week had forecast a 4.5 percent drop in the nominal figure. The nominal figures take no account of inflation.

The TDB said in a statement the decline in exports was largely due to continuing problems in the electronics industry, which accounts for around half Singapore's manufacturing output and approaching 60 percent of its non-oil exports.

"Though it was less severe than the 7.9 percent contraction in the previous month, it reflected continued weakness in the global demand for some electronics and related products such as semi-conductors," the statement said.

The TDB said non-oil sales to the United States decreased by 10.6 percent to S$2.1 billion in March. It said the decrease was reflected in domestic exports of disk drives, computer parts and peripherals and other electronics goods.
Non-oil exports to the European Union rose 4.9 percent to S$1.6 billion, while exports to Malaysia increased by 2.7 percent to S$1.0 billion.
